A cow is a large, four-legged farm animal with hooves, a thick body, a long tail, and — in many cases — horns. You've almost certainly seen one, or at least a picture of one: a big, gentle creature that grazes on grass in fields and meadows.

But here's something important: technically, the word "cow" refers specifically to an adult female of the cattle species. Not just any cattle — the female one, specifically one that has already given birth at least once. Before she gives birth for the first time, she's called a heifer. Once she has a calf (a baby), she becomes a cow.

The males are called bulls. The young ones (male or female) are called calves. A castrated male is called a steer. The whole group together — bulls, cows, calves, steers — is called cattle.
But in everyday speech, it's used more loosely

In real-world conversation, most people use "cow" casually to mean any member of the cattle species, male or female. If you point at a field full of cattle and say "Look at those cows," nobody will correct you. This loose, everyday use is perfectly normal and understood everywhere.

So the word works on two levels:

  • Strict/technical meaning: adult female cattle
  • Informal/everyday meaning: cattle in general

Cows are one of the most important domesticated animals in human history. They are kept primarily for:

  • Milk — which is also turned into butter, cheese, yogurt, cream, and other dairy products
  • Meat — beef comes from cattle; veal comes from very young calves
  • Labour — in many parts of the world, cattle (including cows) are used to pull ploughs and carts
  • Leather — their hide is used to make leather goods
  • Dung — used as fertilizer and, in some regions, as fuel

A single cow can produce a remarkable amount of milk — often thousands of litres per year — which is why dairy farming has been central to human agriculture for thousands of years.

This is a detail many learners don't know: the word "cow" isn't only for cattle. It is also used for the adult female of several other large animals. For example:

  • A female elephant is called a cow.
  • A female whale is called a cow.
  • A female hippopotamus is called a cow.
  • A female moose is called a cow.
  • A female bison (also called a buffalo) is called a cow.
  • A female seal or walrus is also called a cow.

So when you see the word "cow," context matters. "A cow elephant" means a female elephant. In most everyday situations, though, "cow" without any additional word means a cattle cow.

In informal British English (and to some extent in Australian and Irish English), "cow" is sometimes used as a mild insult for a woman considered to be unpleasant, unkind, or difficult. For example: "She was a real cow to me today." This usage is considered rude, though not extremely offensive. It is not really used this way in American English. Be aware of this meaning so you're not confused when you encounter it, but avoid using it yourself, as it is unkind.

The standard plural is cows. However, when speaking about the species as a whole — all cattle together — people often just say cattle (which has no singular form on its own). "Cattle" is always plural. You'd say "the cattle are grazing," never "a cattle."

There is also an older, poetic plural — kine — but this is archaic and almost never used today except in literature.

"Until the cows come home" is a well-known English idiom meaning for a very long time, possibly forever. It comes from the image of cows slowly wandering back to the barn at the end of the day — there's no rushing them. Example: "You could argue about this until the cows come home and still not reach an agreement."

SituationWhat "cow" means

In short: A cow is most precisely an adult female cattle animal. Casually, it refers to cattle in general. It's also the correct word for the adult female of elephants, whales, moose, hippos, and bison. In farming, cows are valued above all for their milk and meat. In British informal speech, it can serve as a mild insult for a disagreeable woman. And "until the cows come home" means for an indefinitely long time.

That covers everything you need to know about this word.
